verses.1: After all the words he had spoken were heard by the people, he went into Kafarnaum.
verses.2: A slave of a centurion, who was being mistreated by someone who was supposed to be his master, was about to die.
verses.3: After hearing about Jesus, some of the Jews sent another messenger to him, asking him to come and save their slave.
verses.4: But those who came before Jesus praised him greatly, saying that it was right for him to go there.
verses.5: For our people truly love us, and it is through their unity that they have built us together.
verses.6: But Jesus went with them. Soon after he left the house, the centurion sent his friends to say to him, “Lord, don’t carry it too far; I’m not worthy to enter my house.”
verses.7: Therefore, I didn’t dare to go to you myself. But I spoke to you through words. May my child be blessed.
verses.8: And indeed, as a human being, I am subject to authority. I have soldiers under my command. And I say to this one: “Go ahead, and do it.” To the other one: “Come here, and do it too.” To my slave: “Create something from this, and do it.”
verses.9: When Jesus heard this, he was amazed at him. Then, as he continued to walk with the crowd, he said, “I tell you, even in Israel, no one has ever seen such faith.”
verses.10: And when they entered the house, those who had been sent there found the slave to be healthy.
verses.11: And in that journey, he went to a city called Nain. His disciples and a large crowd accompanied him on this journey.
verses.12: But when he entered the gates of the city, he saw that a single son of his mother was being brought out. His mother was a widow, and the people of the city were also with her.
verses.13: And when the Lord saw her, he became angry with her and said to her, “Do not cry.”
verses.14: And when he came forward, he poured the salt on it. Those who were standing nearby stood up, and he said, “Young man, I tell you, get up.”
verses.15: And the dead man sat up and began to speak. He gave him back to his mother.
verses.16: He brought fear upon all people. They praised the God, saying that a great prophet had arisen among them. They also said that God had guided his people.
verses.17: And this message spread throughout all of Judea, about him and about all the surrounding areas.
verses.18: And his disciples reported to John about all these things. So, inviting two of his disciples, John…
verses.19: He sent a message to the Lord, saying: “Are you indeed the one who will come, or do we expect someone else?”
verses.20: Then the men who were with him said, “John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying, ‘Is it you who are coming or someone else?’”
verses.21: In that time, he cured many people from diseases and illnesses such as acne and respiratory problems. He also helped many blind people to regain their ability to see again.
verses.22: And he replied to them, “When you go, tell John what you have seen and heard. The blind will see, the sick will be healed, the deaf will hear, the dead will rise, and the poor will be saved.”
verses.23: And it is better if he does not get upset with me.
verses.24: When the messengers of John arrived, they began to speak to the crowd about John. “Why have you come into the wilderness to be tempted? To suffer under the wind’s blows?”
verses.25: But why did you come to see me? A man wrapped in thin clothes, right? Those who are respected and favored in the royal courts are indeed those who are wrapped in such thin clothes.
verses.26: But why have you come to see a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and even more so, a prophet.
verses.27: This is about what is written here. Now, I will send my messenger before your face, so that he can prepare the path ahead for you.
verses.28: I say to you, none of the women born to John is greater in significance than any other woman. But the youngest among them is indeed greater in importance than all the others in the kingdom of God.
verses.29: And when all the people heard this, they also praised God, after being baptized by John’s baptism.
verses.30: But the Pharisees and those who were religious also regarded the council of God as nothing more than a mere formality, since they themselves weren’t baptized by it.
verses.31: In what way can I make people similar to each other in terms of their lineage? And in what ways are they similar?
verses.32: They are like children who sit in the market and exchange gifts with each other. This is what it means: “We have wept for you, but you did not cry out; we have mourned for you, but you did not console us.”
verses.33: For John the Baptist refused to eat or drink. You say that he has been possessed by demons.
verses.34: The son of man was given the ability to eat and drink. And you say, “Look! A man who eats and drinks, a friend of gluttons and sinners.”
verses.35: And wisdom was granted to all his sons.
verses.36: Then someone from the Pharisees asked him to eat with them. When he went into the Pharisee’s house, he was arrested.
verses.37: And behold, there was a woman who was a sinner in that city. She knew that she was living in the house of the Pharisee. So, she took some honey and put it on her tongue.
verses.38: And she cried out in pain as she tried to get away from his feet. He began to wash her feet with tears, and he also removed the dirt from her head. Then he wrapped her feet in bandages.
verses.39: When the Pharisee who invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know what kind of woman this is who looks at him; for she is a sinner.”
verses.40: And after answering, Jesus said to him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He replied, “Teacher, please say what it is.”
verses.41: There were two debtors who owed money to a certain creditor. One of them owed five hundred denarii, while the other owed fifty denarii.
verses.42: Not accepting their surrender, he was filled with joy. Who among them would love him more than the others?
verses.43: After answering, Simon said, “I believe that you have judged rightly.” But he replied, “You have indeed judged correctly.”
verses.44: And Simon, who was with his wife, said to her, “Do you see this woman? When she entered your house, you didn’t give me any water to drink. But she wiped my feet with her tears and washed them with her saliva.”
verses.45: I didn’t give you my love; but she, since we entered together, never stopped caressing my feet.
verses.46: You didn’t hurt my head with a nail; instead, it used a nail to hurt my feet.
verses.47: For this reason, I say to you, many of her sins will be forgiven, because she loved too much. But those who love less will have fewer sins forgiven.
verses.48: He said to her, “Forgive your sins.”
verses.49: And those who were around them began to talk among themselves. “Who is this person who comes among the sinners?”
verses.50: He said to his wife, “Your faith has saved you. Go forward and seek peace.”
